title: How to Add a Legend to a Doughnut Chart in Creatio Freedom UI Using JavaScript? | Community Creatio
text: Question How_to_Add_a_Legend_to_a_Doughnut_Chart_in_Creatio_Freedom_UI_Using_JavaScript? Studio_Creatio_enterprise_edition 8.0 How to Add a Legend to a Doughnut Chart in Creatio Freedom UI Using JavaScript? Chetana Gharat 11:22 Oct 10, 2026 How to Add a Legend to a Doughnut Chart in Creatio Freedom UI Using JavaScript? Hi Creatio Community, I'm working on a doughnut chart in Creatio Freedom UI and would like to display a legend below the chart. However, the chart configuration available in the Freedom UI designer does not provide an option to enable the legend for a doughnut chart. I would like to explore whether this can be achieved through a client-side JavaScript handler without modifying the underlying chart configuration or affecting the chart's existing functionality. Chart element: HTML inside the ts-chart component Requirement: Display a custom legend below the doughnut chart, showing each series' actual color and label. Questions: Is there a supported way to enable or configure a legend for a doughnut chart in Creatio Freedom UI? If the designer does not support this option, can a custom legend be added using a Freedom UI client-side JavaScript handler? How can we access the chart's actual labels, dataset values, and colors from the ts-chart component or its underlying chart configuration? Is there a recommended or supported API for accessing the chart instance without relying on undocumented internal properties? My preference is to display the legend below the doughnut chart, using the existing chart labels and colors, while keeping the implementation scoped to this widget and preserving its existing interactions. Any guidance, examples, or recommended approaches would be appreciated. Thank you! Like 0 Like 1 comments Oleg Drobina 11:58 Oct 12, 2026 Like 0 Hi, Thank you for the detailed question. Here are answers to each point, followed by the approach we recommend. 1. Is there a supported way to enable a legend for a doughnut chart? Unfortunately, no. This is a current platform limitation, not a setting the Freedom UI Designer is missing. The Show legend option is available only for Spline, Line, Bar, Area, Column and Scatter charts. Pie and doughnut charts don’t support a legend. If you add a legend setting to the doughnut series by editing the page schema, the page saves it, but no legend appears. The chart turns off the legend for pie, doughnut, funnel and waterfall charts. You can’t set slice colors either. The series color property is ignored for doughnut charts, and slices take their colors from the built-in palette. What doughnut charts do show is a “label – NN%” data label next to each slice by default. Long labels wrap. Labels that would overlap are hidden, so very small slices may have no label. The dataLabel.display setting has no effect on doughnut charts. 2. Can a custom legend be added with client-side code? Yes, as a separate element placed directly under the chart . title: ESQ Transactions | Community Creatio
text: Question ESQ_Transaction ESQ Transactions Krzysztof 17:50 Oct 09, 2026 Hello Community, I have a question if its possible to have database transaction scope using ESQ instead of direct SQL. From the documentation it is suggested that we as Devs should use ESQ most of the times because of validation etc. I have a case where I have to modify two entities and for that I need two separate ESQ (maybe there is a better way). My goal is to wrap that in a single transaction so that all changes are made or none (to avoid inconsistency). Is this code below valid for this case? Is going to work? ``` using System; using Terrasoft.Core.DB; using Terrasoft.Core.Entities; using (DBExecutor dbExecutor = UserConnection.EnsureDBConnection()) { dbExecutor.StartTransaction(); try { var schemaManager = UserConnection.EntitySchemaManager; // Contact Entity contact = schemaManager.GetInstanceByName("Contact").CreateEntity(UserConnection); contact.SetDefColumnValues(); contact.SetColumnValue("Name", "Jane Doe"); contact.Save(); // Case, linked to the new contact Entity supportCase = schemaManager.GetInstanceByName("Case").CreateEntity(UserConnection); supportCase.SetDefColumnValues(); supportCase.SetColumnValue("Subject", "Test case"); supportCase.SetColumnValue("ContactId", contact.PrimaryColumnValue); supportCase.Save(); // ...more entities as needed dbExecutor.CommitTransaction(); } catch { dbExecutor.RollbackTransaction(); throw; } } ``` Thanks for all answers. Like 1 Like 2 comments Best reply Oleg Drobina 12:29 Oct 11, 2026 Like 0 Hi, Yes, this pattern works, and Creatio’s own core code uses it (sync, process completion, AppManager). Using Entity here is correct. ESQ is mainly for reading data; Entity , or Insert / Update queries, are the right tools for writing. Why it works UserConnection.EnsureDBConnection() doesn’t open a new connection each time. It returns the DBExecutor cached on that UserConnection and adds one to a reference count. Entity.Save() calls UserConnection.EnsureDBConnection() internally, so it gets the same executor. Every command that executor runs is enlisted in its open transaction. That covers more than the main INSERT/UPDATE: default record rights, owner rights, localization rows, change tracking, and DB writes made by synchronous event handlers on the same UserConnection . Save() doesn’t start its own transaction on insert or update. Delete() does, but transactions nest with a depth counter. An inner Commit or Rollback does nothing, so only your outermost call decides. If the using block ends without a commit (for example, an unexpected exception), Dispose() rolls the transaction back. Your explicit RollbackTransaction() is still good practice. Things to watch for Save() can return false without throwing. This happens when an OnSaving , OnInserting or OnUpdating handler cancels the save. Your try block would then commit the other entities. Check the return value. Use the same UserConnection for everything. Work done through SystemUserConn

title: Business Process won't run open specific page | Community Creatio
text: Question Studio_Creatio 8.0 Business Process won't run open specific page Kevin Samuel 13:49 Oct 08, 2026 Hi, I want to open specific page via business process. The button was clicked from mobile and it will run the business process. I checked the execution diagram and it seems worked. However the mobile does nothing and it seems stucked. Like 0 Like 1 comments Oleg Drobina 10:40 Oct 09, 2026 Like 1 Hi, Your process is probably fine. What fails is the hand-off at “Open edit page”: the Creatio mobile app most likely never handles the message that tells a client to open the page. So the process sits waiting on that element, which is why the diagram looks right while the phone does nothing. How to confirm In the process log, check the “Buka detail halaman…” element. If it shows “in progress” rather than “completed”, the process is waiting for a client that never answers. Press the same button in the web app as the same user. If the page opens there, the problem is mobile-only. Optionally, keep a browser tab open as that user and press the button on the phone. If the page pops up in the browser, the phone is just ignoring the message. Check your Creatio version. Starting a process from a Freedom UI mobile button ( crt.RunBusinessProcessRequest ) is only supported in Creatio Mobile 8.3.4 and later ( Academy handlers reference ). How to fix it: let the process do data only, and do the navigation on the mobile side A (recommended): no process. Bind the button to a mobile custom request handler, built with @creatio/mobile-common and the EnableMobileSDK feature ( overview ). The handler: looks up the record by No Prospect; if it’s found, opens it with crt.UpdateRecordRequest (or crt.OpenPageRequest ); if not, opens a new record with crt.CreateRecordRequest , with No Prospect pre-filled. A handler written for the web (a usr.* schema handler) won’t work on mobile. B (8.3.4 and later): keep the process, but only for data. Remove both “Open edit page” elements and keep Read Data / Add Data. Start the process with crt.RunBusinessProcessRequest , then open the record from the mobile side. C (before 8.3.4): start the process from a record change. Have the button set a field, and let a signal-started process do the data work. Navigation still has to happen on the mobile side. If the web test (step 2) also fails: the process may be running in background mode, from a background or batch connection, or with “Show execution page” turned off. In those cases the server skips sending the message entirely and the symptom looks the same. Also cancel the runs already stuck on “Open edit page” in the process log so they don’t pile up. title: How can I add data source in Mobile Page ? | Community Creatio
text: Question mobile application adddatasource Studio_Creatio 8.0 How can I add data source in Mobile Page ? Dedi Sadikin 12:40 Oct 07, 2026 Hi All, Question please, how can I add data source in Mobile Page? I googling, and Creatio said it should be in the left top corner, link : https://academy.creatio.com/guides/mobile/mobile-app-setup/freedom-ui/freedom-ui-mobile-designer Need advice please, thank you. Like 0 Like 1 comments Oleg Drobina 16:15 Oct 07, 2026 Like 0 Hi, Why you don't see the button One data source per page. The guide says "Each mobile page works with a single data source." In your screenshot, the VERIFICATION group in the Components panel is that data source. Its fields appear under Data model attributes (A. Age, A. CIF No, and so on). The button is only for pages that don't have one yet. You get Add data source → New data source (then Name and Description) when you create a mobile page from a template that has no data source. Creatio then creates a new object and connects it to the page. Your form page was created from the existing app, so it was bound to the Verification object automatically. Version. This designer feature needs Creatio 8.3.2 or later. If you're on an older version, the button won't be there at all. What you can do instead Add fields to the current data source. In the VERIFICATION group, use the Add new field tiles (Text, Number, Dropdown, …) or drag existing attributes from Data model attributes onto the page. Show data from another object. Mobile pages share data sources with their desktop Freedom UI pages: "data sources configured for a Freedom UI page are automatically available on the corresponding Freedom UI mobile page." Open the desktop Verification form page in the Freedom UI Designer, add the extra data source there (for example, a list or detail of related records), save it, then reopen the mobile designer. Use a separate object as the main source. Create a new mobile page from a template. That's where Add data source appears. Also note that the Academy page recommends the Freedom UI Mobile Designer only for newly created apps, not for adding mobile pages to apps that already existed. If "Mobile Survey" is an older app, that may explain other limitations you run into.
